header.title: Level 3: the curve book
header.briefing: Clients ask in the 2Y, 5Y, 10Y and 30Y. Your risk is a curve, not a number: price each request by what it does to the WHOLE book, then decide where (and whether) to hedge. Limits: total DV01, and slope exposure.

risk_card.title: Training assumptions (a simplified model for this exercise, not estimates of true market volatility)

conditions.flow: corporate hedging season: corporates are paying 5-10Y to fix floating-rate debt; bank treasuries are two-way at the front.

inquiry.description: Bank treasury managing its balance-sheet hedge
inquiry.short: bank treasury managing its balance-sheet hedge

observation.prompt: Your rate for the client to pay at (or 'pass')?

reasons: Passing keeps you inside your limits.

conditions.flow: corporate hedging season: corporates are paying 5-10Y to fix floating-rate debt; bank treasuries are two-way at the front.

last_inquiry.short: bank treasury managing its balance-sheet hedge

input.hint: 'none'; '100% 10y' (of your DV01); 'flatten' (level, slope and curvature); or legs: 'pay 150m 10y + receive 60m 30y'

reasons: A reasonable trade-off for a reasonable risk appetite. For a middle-of-the-range appetite the best balance is: hedge level and curve (2y + 30y).
Your choice: cost now €19,787, risk over the next step sigma €30,579 (keeping the book as it is: sigma €120,141).
